discovery: Precision mapping of the cosmic microwave background anisotropies, establishing the standard cosmological model and the nearly scale-invariant spectrum of primordial fluctuations

nominees.name: David N. Spergel
nominees.affiliation: Simons Foundation and Princeton University, USA

nominees.name: Jean-Loup Puget
nominees.affiliation: Institut d'Astrophysique Spatiale, CNRS / Université Paris-Saclay, France

motivation: The WMAP and Planck satellites turned cosmology into a precision science. Bennett led WMAP, whose full-sky temperature and polarization maps measured the acoustic peak structure. Spergel led its cosmological interpretation, fixing the geometry, matter and baryon content and the age of the Universe to percent precision. Puget conceived and led Planck's High Frequency Instrument. Its cosmic-variance-limited temperature maps, polarization and lensing reconstructions confirmed the six-parameter LambdaCDM model at sub-percent level and detected the departure from scale invariance (n_s ≈ 0.965) at more than 8 sigma. That is direct evidence for adiabatic, Gaussian primordial perturbations, as inflation predicts. These experiments also put strong limits on neutrino masses, the number of relativistic species and primordial gravitational waves. With careful control of systematics and foregrounds, they made the CMB the most rigorous laboratory for fundamental physics on cosmological scales.
